extracted.intended_audience: readers of Victorian humorous sketches / general readers of satire
extracted.subtask_description: A satirical, short fictional sketch in the style of Charles Dickens (Sketches by Boz) reporting comic episodes, mock‑scientific societies, and absurd inventions. The piece mixes narrated travel/journal reporting with scene sketches and parodic minutes of meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of the correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: For faithfulness of description, power of language, fervour of thought, happiness of expression, and importance of subject-matter, have no equal in the epistolary literature of any age or country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enumerates desirable qualities for the letters/reports being published: faithful description; strong language; fervent thinking; felicitous expression; and significant subject‑matter. Used here as praise of the reporter’s style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish correspondence entire and in received order
rubrics_metrics.description: We give this gentleman’s correspondence entire, and in the order in which it reached our office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial principle: present a correspondent’s letters whole and chronologically as received rather than excerpting or reordering, to preserve authenticity and narrative flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record impressions immediately to preserve vividness
rubrics_metrics.description: I write down these remarks as they occur to me, or as the facts come to my knowledge, in order that my first impressions may lose nothing of their original vividness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical reporting/journal style guidance: note impressions contemporaneously; avoid heavy retrospection so that initial vividness and spontaneity remain in the account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispatch short packets as opportunities arise
rubrics_metrics.description: I shall despatch them in small packets as opportunities arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial/serial publication guidance: send or publish short dispatches (small packets) frequently rather than waiting for a single long report—useful for travelogues and serialized sketches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronological, comprehensive first-person reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: I am the first passenger on board, and shall thus be enabled to give you an account of all that happens in the order of its occurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts a reporting desideratum: a first‑person observer who is present early can provide a sequential, comprehensive account; implies value in chronological narrative structure for reader comprehension and humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support provenance claims with proper definition/evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The President wished to know what botanical definition the honourable gentleman could afford of the curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming botanical (or other factual) provenance — e.g., that a twig is a genuine shoot of 'Shakspeare' — be prepared to provide a proper scientific/definitional basis or evidence rather than relying on anecdote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit performance claims for inventions (demonstrable benchmarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: A machine...by the aid of which more pockets could be picked in one hour than by the present slow and tedious process in four-and-twenty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventor should state clear, testable performance metrics (here: pockets picked per hour vs. current rate). The passage also notes social and adoption concerns (practitioners objecting due to job loss) and the possible need to apply to Parliament for recognition/adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automaton police design/specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: An automaton police force...which...would walk about until knocked down like any real man; nay, more, if set upon and beaten...the figure would utter divers groans, mingled with entreaties for mercy...magistrates will have wooden heads of course, and they will be made of the toughest and thickest materials...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satirical but specific design criteria for an amusement automaton: durability (tough wooden heads), lifelike behaviour (able to walk, be knocked down, groan and plead), reusability (can be repaired/returned to service), organized deployment (divisions lettered A–G, half on active duty, remainder shelved). Also includes requirements for a pantomimic investigation and token/counter‑based fines as part of the amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magistrates/automata should talk (interactive/audible behaviour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Professor Nogo.—I see but one objection to it. It appears to me that the magistrates ought to talk. ... one of the figures immediately began to exclaim with great volubility that he was sorry to see gentlemen in such a situation, and the other to express a fear that the policeman was intoxicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design expectation that automata acting as magistrates should produce speech/playable lines to complete the illusion — i.e., audible, scripted interaction is a desired feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic/mysterious construction can be a virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Prosee...declared it to be so ingeniously composed, that he was wholly unable to discover how it went on at all. Mr. Blank.—Nobody can, and that is the beauty of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For certain exhibited models or fashionable objects, an air of ingenious mystery (not readily explainable) is presented as a positive quality: inscrutability itself may be praised as part of an object's appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design specs for leisure/amusement ground for nobility
rubrics_metrics.description: A space...not less than ten miles in length and four in breadth...laid out with highway roads, turnpikes, bridges, miniature villages...houses of entertainment...streets of door-knockers and bell-handles of extra size...gas lamps of real glass...a broad and handsome foot pavement...live pedestrians would be procured from the workhouse...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satirical blueprint for an exclusive amusement park: scale, constructed features for staged activities, purposely breakable or detachable fittings for sport, and contrived human actors (procured from institutions) to create the desired experience. Implicit criteria: realism, controlled exclusivity, and provision for staged disorder as entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive ideas should be argued from plausible principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Tickle displayed his newly-invented spectacles...based strictly upon the principle of the human eye. The President required some information upon this point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventors are expected to ground their contrivances in an articulated principle (here, analogy to the human eye). The President’s scepticism suggests that plausibility and explanatory grounding matter for credibility in a scientific/modeled exhibition.
